Lead multi-team programs end to end, including integrated plans, critical paths, and phased global rollouts to site teams
Define and enforce stage gates and readiness criteria (design, security review, pilot, production)
Ensure programs conform to approved architecture and engineering standards, working closely with architecture and review boards
Run program governance, including steering committees, status cadences, RAID logs, and decision records
Creates clarity from complexity by turning strategy, competing priorities, and incomplete information into an executable roadmap
Balances pace, cost, technical quality, cybersecurity, and long-term supportability in program decisions

Manage vendor and integrator engagements, including SOWs, deliverables, and performance
Track benefits realization and report whether delivered programs achieved their intended outcomes.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, technology, or a related field is desired.

Support budgeting, forecasting, expense monitoring, compliance activities, workforce and business planning processes
Monitor, track and report operational performance against targets
Conduct analysis, maintain data and develop comprehensive reports, dashboards and other tools to assist with and support business decisions and risk mitigation objectives
Support vendor, contract, inventory, asset and space management
Provide analysis for improvement projects, assist with problem solving, planning and execution
Identify and implement cost reduction opportunities

Performance Optimization & Continuous Improvement

Ensure work activities are completed in accordance with established standards, procedures, and documentation requirements

About Us

At Winston Taylor, we set the standard, together.

Winston Taylor is a transatlantic law firm built for the businesses, people, and markets driving capital and innovation. Here, you're in the room. In the action. Sleeves rolled up. You'll work with leading clients. Disruptors. Fast-growth companies. And help them to stay one step ahead of the moment and make critical decisions that shape their future. We're present in the U.S., U.K., Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East, combining the scale and speed that clients demand. You'll be trusted with real responsibility from the outset and build experience through hands-on work. We take your progression personally. We provide the platform. You shape the work around your goals and aspirations. Step into the moments that matter. Join Winston Taylor.

Position Summary

Winston Taylor’s Project Management Office (PMO) has a wide scope of responsibilities, including initiatives across the firm’s global departments and practices. This role partners with both staff and attorney stakeholders to scope, plan, and manage medium to high complexity projects on a global scale – including but not limited to: business process improvements, office moves, technology product implementations, and business development special projects. It is responsible for the creation and delivery of project plans that support business solutions and to meet the firm’s evolving needs by improving current processes. In addition, this role will serve as the liaison between the customer community and the technical teams, ensuring that documented requirements are implemented to the project stakeholder’s satisfaction.

The project management team has regular engagement with top firm leadership and is expected to play a meaningful role in executing on business and technology initiatives that impact the Firm’s clients, the Firm’s competitiveness, and the quality of working environment for all employees. Therefore, each project manager on this team is critical and is expected to meaningfully define and drive progress, not just passively establish and document meetings.

Position Responsibilities

Partner with project sponsors or subject matter experts to identify and document a project’s business requirements with a focus on increasing business effectiveness and efficiencies, including development of project feasibility and cost-benefit analyses.
Lead and facilitate project meetings ensuring effective and timely communication across the project team, especially among project stakeholders and PMO leadership.
Prepare project charters and project plans and deliver projects within allocated time and resource targets to satisfy the defined scope and quality.
Identify risks, manage scope changes and resource constraints, and develop mitigation strategies as needed.
Drive decision-making and escalation among project stakeholders, PMO leadership, and firm leadership, when appropriate.
Continuously improve upon existing project management methodology. Assist with the expansion of the firm’s project management methodology, best practices, and tools
Prepare recommendations for technological and business solutions based on project requirements.
Develop and maintain project objective(s), scope, and work plan related to software development, implementations of new or modified applications, and business processes.
Communicate with project teams and management regarding the status of all ongoing projects including project issues and accomplishments. Ensure completion of project deliverables based on identified requirements and approved timeline.
Work closely with the Quality Assurance Manager and Business Analyst roles to monitor and track defects (including gaps from stakeholder requirements or ease of use) identified during testing through resolution.
Work closely with Change Managers to support organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and adoption activities, ensuring successful implementation and sustained realization of project objectives.
Coordinate project rollout to the user community, including communications, documentation, reference guides and demonstrations.
Understand integrations between all applications/systems maintained by the Firm.
Research and analyze new technologies. Maintain professional and technical knowledge by attending educational workshops, reviewing professional publications, and establishing personal networks.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience, Skills, And Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree is required.
3+ years of project management experience in a law firm or relevant professional services environment required.
Must live within a commutable distance to a firm office with ability to come into the office 3-4 days per week.
Advanced knowledge of project management methodologies and tools.
Strong leadership, prioritization, and organization skills.
Ability to develop and maintain ongoing relationships with firm leadership, customers, stakeholders, and project sponsors.
Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to present detailed or complicated information in an understandable way to firm attorneys and staff.
Strong information gathering and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated ability to apply critical thinking to complex situations.
Experience working with and collaborating among interdisciplinary teams to identify and solve complex business problems.
Experience managing projects associated with mergers, acquisitions, and organizational integrations, including coordination of cross-functional teams, dependencies, risks, and business transition activities.
Skilled in conveying business requirements to the appropriate business leaders and/or IS team members and, where necessary, with vendors.
Capable of overseeing technical creation and implementation of business solutions.
Experience with testing to ensure completion of project deliverables.
Experience in information systems and/or applying technology solutions to business processes.
Experience with non-US operations especially in Europe and Asia are beneficial.

Our expertise includes full service-capabilities, resourcing and Functional Service (FSP) solutions.

Join Our Team as a Project Manager [1.0 FTE] - (home based in US).

About This Role

As part of our CDS Ophthalmology
teams you will be working alongside passionate and innovative professionals to ensure our customers achieve their goals.
The Project Manager
will plan and pro-actively manage multidisciplinary study teams (including Site Management, Data Management, Statistics, Medical Writing, Regulatory and Safety) to ensure key milestones are achieved and studies are performed within budget, on schedule and in compliance with the appropriate - and quality standards.

Key Responsibilities

Ensure that projects are delivered on-time, within scope and within budget and in compliance with applicable quality standards.
Manages the strategic aspects of projects, identify, analyze and minimize/mitigates any risk, including the implications of difference technical and operational choices.
Communicates effectively with clients to successfully manage the relationship, identify needs and evaluate alternative business solutions and strategies.
Develop and maintain Project Plans and timelines for their project and track progress.
Ensure all study team members -are adequately trained on project specific systems and procedures.
Implements, and maintains sound business practices.
Measure and evaluate project performance.
Manage the project budget, profitability and ensure invoicing is performed on time and in accordance with the scope of work.
Working with the Finance & Accounting team to analyze profitability, revenue, margins and utilization across their projects..
Manage the resource allocation, on the project, in collaboration with respective line managers.
Facilitate internal and external communication.
Report and escalate to management as needed.
Establish and maintain relationship with third parties/vendors.
Manages high-level deliverables across the organization.
Participate in capability presentations/bid defenses, as needed.
Continually defines ways to increase customer satisfaction and deepen client relationships.
Contribute in review/develop procedures, guidelines, SOPs, metrics as needed

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree, preferably in life science or RN diploma.
3 year of relevant experience in clinical research.
Knowledge of clinical research regulations governing the conduct of the clinical trials and quality standards.
Understanding of project planning and metrics.
Ability to lead and manage staff.
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
Solid organizational skills and ability to prioritize.
Internal and external negotiation skills.
Ability and willingness to travel to 10%

What We Offer

We provide a competitive compensation package, comprehensive benefits and the opportunity for personal and professional growth in a rewarding environment. You’ll be joining a team that values collaboration, innovation, and making a difference in the lives of patients

Our journey began over 30 years ago in Sweden, in the city of Lund. As a full-service, global Contract Research Organization (CRO), we build solution-driven teams working towards a healthier future. Company Description

Galileo Learning’s mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world.

We provide out-of-school enrichment programs that build innovation skills, growth mindset, and creative confidence across a variety of offerings. We run neighborhood summer day camps for families, deliver expanded learning programs for school districts, and empower educational institutions and service providers with curriculum and instructional support.

We bring our mission to life through the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA): combining mindset, process, and knowledge to drive meaningful outcomes for students and for each other. This shows up in how we collaborate, make decisions, and continuously improve our work.

We Are

Visionary: We think beyond what exists today and work toward what’s possible.
Courageous: We take ownership, make decisions with imperfect information, and lean into challenges.
Collaborative: We work across teams and perspectives, assuming positive intent and building strong partnerships.
Determined: We follow through, hold a high bar for quality, and stay focused on delivering results that matter for our students and partners
Reflective: We learn from experience, use data and feedback to improve, and continuously evolve how we work.

We operate with a high level of ownership and care for our work, our partners, and each other.

Job Description

Galileo is looking for an experienced leader to join our team as a Field Program Manager. As Galileo grows our presence and sites throughout Orange County, this role will be instrumental in partnering with district expanded learning programs and creating a best-in-class staff experience for our Camp Directors and summer staff. The Field Program Manager will support camp operations and marketing across the region. An ideal candidate will be passionate about and experienced with bringing programming to under-served communities and inspired by Galileo’s potential impact.

You will be Accountable For

Drive operational excellence across a portfolio of sites throughout the greater Orange County region, partnering with district leadership to provide impact-driven ELOP services in under-served communities.
Manage a team of Camp Directors; creating professional development opportunities, giving timely feedback, and ensuring safe, welcoming staff teams that value belonging, joy, and camp innovation & fun.
Partnering with the Area Director, develop camp operating plans for each managed site and train Camp Directors on all logistics and operations. Manage Camp Directors to execute day to day site logistics and partnership on site.
In partnership with the L&D team, develop content for training Camp Directors, including facilitating retreat logistics and content, developing coaching materials, and deploying coaching capacity across sites.
Foster relationships in the community through networking and building relationships with district and school site partners and families.
Serve as an escalation point for your team on issues or challenges that they do not feel prepared to resolve on their own; assist in resolution that balances customer care and program needs.
Monitor and respond to feedback from district partners and staff based on on-site observation–to identify and mitigate challenges and performance gaps.
Partner with our People Operations Team to hire, onboard, train, and support our Camp Director team throughout the hiring process and the pre-camp season.
Serve as the cross-departmental partner with marketing, customer service, training, the people operations department, and the supply team to identify and implement customizations to existing operations based on district needs.
In partnership with Account Manager, refine KPIs for each camp and capture performance data.

YOU ARE

Strategic, organized and performance-driven. Problem-solving makes you downright giddy. You look at the details of life through a lens of optimization, measurement, and efficiency and feel responsible for getting things done.
Adaptable and action-oriented. You can manage a variety of projects simultaneously. Changing deadlines? Multiple stakeholders? Easy breezy. You manage your time well and are meticulous about the details.
A visionary collaborator. You can confidently contribute to a creative vision and have the team-oriented mindset to work with others to realize it effectively.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
Experience in multi-site staff management and managing programs or services
Experience with marketing and community communications preferred
Minimum 2 years experience working with K-8 education; experience working at camps and/or out-of-school time programs a bonus
Minimum 3 years experience managing individuals and a team
Experience with staff hiring, recruiting, training, development, and feedback a must
Ability to travel in and around the Greater Orange County region
Experience with B2B sales or account management is a plus

We strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and we are committed to equitable and inclusive hiring practices. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply!

Work Location

This role is primarily remote, work-from-home, based out of Orange County.

HQ staff may be expected to visit camp locations or clients to experience Camp Galileo and Galileo X Solutions first-hand. Occasionally, onsite events or meetings may also be required. 10-15% travel may be required, depending on location.

Schedule & Time Commitment

This is a full-time position, averaging 40 hours per week. While we prioritize work-life balance, there may be times when additional hours are necessary to meet deadlines and ensure the success of our programs.

Compensation

We anticipate the compensation for this full-time, exempt, position to be $80,000 - $90,000. Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and professional experience.

Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Generous parental leave and extensive support with leave planning
Employee Assistance Program, options for life insurance, and more!

We comply with the ADA and provide reasonable accommodations that allow qualified applicants/employees to perform the essential functions of the job. To request an accommodation, contact our Human Resources team.

new_jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend
is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Job Description

Turner & Townsend is seeking an ambitious Project Controls Manager
to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is an experienced construction professional with expertise in project controls, cost management, scheduling, governance, and portfolio reporting on large-scale capital projects and programs.

This role will serve as a key member of the Program Management Office (PMO), providing oversight of project controls processes, governance frameworks, financial performance, budgeting, forecasting, risk management, and reporting across multiple projects. The Project Controls Manager will partner closely with project managers, cost managers, construction managers, contractors, and client stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered within approved budgets, schedules, and governance requirements.

What You'll Do

Project Controls & Governance

Provide PMO oversight and establish project governance processes, controls standards, reporting frameworks, and performance measurement methodologies.
Ensure compliance with client governance requirements, approval processes, and organizational policies.
Present project performance updates, risks, forecasts, and governance recommendations to executive leadership and stakeholders.
Support stage-gate reviews, project approvals, funding requests, and change control governance processes.

Financial Management & Budget Oversight

Oversee project and program budgets, monitoring financial performance including budgets, commitments, expenditures, forecasts, and earned value analysis.
Partner with project managers, cost managers, and contractors to validate financial data and ensure forecast accuracy.
Lead monthly financial reviews and provide executive-level budget reporting with recommendations.
Track project funding, contingency utilization, and evaluate change orders and potential claims for financial impact.
Develop forecasting models and provide early identification of budget risks and opportunities.

Schedule Management

Develop, maintain, and update Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) and consolidate contractor schedules into master program schedules.
Conduct schedule analysis, resource loading, and assess impacts to critical path activities.
Monitor schedule deviations and support development of recovery and mitigation plans.
Facilitate schedule reviews with project teams and conduct quality reviews to ensure schedule integrity.

Reporting, Analytics & Performance Management

Produce monthly, quarterly, and executive-level portfolio reports and dashboards with earned value metrics and KPIs.
Analyze trends, forecasts, and project health metrics to provide actionable recommendations for improved outcomes.
Maintain records of scope changes, risks, opportunities, and performance variances.

Risk & Change Management

Facilitate quantitative risk assessments and schedule risk analyses while maintaining project risk registers.
Lead project change control processes and coordinate stakeholder approvals to ensure governance compliance.

Stakeholder Management & Commercial Support

Interface with project stakeholders as a trusted advisor, facilitating status meetings, financial reviews, and governance sessions.
Support contract administration, procurement processes, and evaluate commercial risks and financial exposure.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Project Management, Finance, Business, or related field.
8+ years of experience in project controls, project management, PMO, construction management, or cost management on large capital projects within a A/E/C environment.
Strong understanding of project governance, PMO functions, stage-gate processes, and portfolio management.

High proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace.
Experience with cloud-based project management and reporting platforms.

Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong leadership, stakeholder management, and executive communication capabilities.
Self-motivated, proactive, and highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Strong oral and written English communication skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with cross-functional teams.
Valid passport with no geographical limitations.

Job ID:
P147047-3439

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

The Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) Program Manager is responsible for the planning, administration and management of safety, health and fire safety programs throughout the hospital to ensure compliance with all applicable local, state and federal laws, regulations and standards concerning environmental health and safety, as well as applicable standards set forth by the Joint Commission(TJC). Ensure compliance with all standards promulgated by all Federal, State and local agencies through developing and implementing environmental management programs, on-site inspection and monitoring programs throughout the organization. Manages interactions with outside agencies and regulatory agency personnel for assigned area.

Essential Functions

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.

Employees must abide by all Joint Commission Requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, patient care, patient rights and ethical treatment, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety and quality programs, sustaining compliance with National Patient Safety Goals, and licensure and health screenings.

Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the hospital's policies and procedures, including its Service Standards and its Code of Conduct.

Advises management and staff regarding safety protocols and procedures to ensure regulatory compliance as mandated by local, state, and federal agencies. Investigates, researches and makes recommendations regarding best practices with respect to health and safety management
Conducts environmental safety rounding and staff training for assigned programs; Conducts fire drills, equipment and emergency evacuation training (as assigned). Conducts life safety inspections for construction projects
Conducts safety inspections and develops safety manual policies and procedures. Provides all aspects of project management relating to occupational safety and health investigations and inspections.
Conducts The Joint Commission (TJC), Fire/Life Safety regulatory compliance audits; Conducts interviews, reviews records and recommends corrective actions and performance improvement opportunities. Responsible for the interpretation, coordination, and enforcement of The Joint Commission (TJC) Safety Standards; maintains regulatory compliance documentation and records.
Develops and conducts mandated Environment of Care (EOC) Audits in ambulatory and/or hospital facilities. Conducts environmental assessments and recommends mitigation methods as warranted.
Develops and presents reports to leadership as required. Provides written reports of the conducted audits. Analyzes and provide report data and report results to management and various committees of the hospital.
Develops, implements and continuously updates safety and environmental health policies and programs to comply with local, state and federal regulations. Identifies, measures and improves environmental health and safety processes.
Identifies personnel, institutional and material resources needed to accomplish program management objectives. Develops and present annual budgetary requirements for assigned environmental program operations.
Manages all aspects of Laser Safety program (as assigned).
Participates with external task forces, committees and agencies related to health and safety management including those at the hospital, local, regional, state and federal levels.
Prepares and reviews reports to identify root causes and recommend corrective actions. Serves as a technical/regulatory resource in assigned program area and the interpretation of analytical data to determine safety, industrial hygiene or environmental remediation control measures, etc.
Responsible for negotiation of compliance issues with regulatory agencies as necessary and track any response to citations/violations should they occur.
Responsible for overall day to day implementation, training, execution and administration of the Environment of Care (EOC), TJC/Fire Safety management plans. Develops and administers budgets and schedules and performance requirements.
Responsible for the development, administration, management and oversight of effective health and safety programs (as assigned) to ensure environmental safety and compliance with all various safety, health and environmental regulations and requirements of accrediting and licensure bodies.
Works in conjunction with OCIP (Owner Controlled Insurance Program) Safety Manager to assist contractors in meeting TJC/EOC Regulatory Compliance Standards.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities as well as possession of any required licenses or certifications is qualifying.

Education:
Bachelor's degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university

Experience:
Four (4) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience

License/Certification:
None

KNOWLEDGE

These are the observable and measurable attributes and skills required to perform successfully the essential functions of the job and are generally demonstrated through qualifying experience, education or licensure/certification.

Ability to foster effective working relationships and build consensus.
Ability to manage complex projects and resources (people, costs, and time) across multiple departments.
Ability to mediate and resolve complex problems and issues.
Ability to provide leadership and influence others.
Ability to speak and write effectively at a level appropriate for the job.
Knowledge of Accident Investigations.
Knowledge of computer systems and software used in functional area.
Knowledge of Federal, State and Local regulatory requirements related to areas of functional responsibility.
Knowledge of new technologies and ability to maintain and stay abreast of updates and changes.
Knowledge of principles and practices of organization, administration, fiscal and personnel management.
Knowledge of TJC-EOC Standards and Auditing.

Physical Requirements

The Physical Requirements and Working Conditions in which the job is typically performed are available from the Occupational Health Department. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

Compensation is based on the level and requirements of the role.

Salary within our ranges may also be determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, location, and abilities, as required by the role, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Typically, new team members join at the minimum to mid salary range.

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll join a global organization at the forefront of clinical research and laboratory science. to lead and coordinate central laboratory activities across clinical trial programs. This is a high-impact role requiring strong operational oversight, cross-functional leadership, and client engagement.

This is a fully remote role supporting our Global Central Laboratories. We welcome applicants from all locations within the US. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship. Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

Role Overview

The Project Manager, Central Labs monitors and manages all aspects of designated clinical trial protocols in Global Central Labs and is accountable for overall project performance and client’s satisfaction by meeting their needs and expectations through the life cycle of the assigned clinical trials.

The Project Manager provides internal consulting on project management issues, identifies opportunities for process and efficiency improvement, acts as chief liaison to the operational personnel of major sponsors, and is responsible for large study programs. Additionally, the Project Manager prepares and maintains process documents and mentors Project Managers.

Role Responsibilities:

Provide oversight and coordination of study initiation. Review, interpret, translate and program study protocols into a complete and accurate database. Communicate with internal departments and external vendors to ensure project requirements are understood, agreed upon, and followed at all times. Facilitate the flow of technical and clinical laboratory information to all stakeholders (investigational sites, sponsors, and non-technical personnel). Consult and utilize, where appropriate, the scientific input of laboratory management and technical staff to assist the client with management of the clinical trial.
Prepare study specification documents and follow their preparation according to budgets and contracts. Maintain at all times an updated study master file with version controls for specifications, budgets, and contracts. Ensure sponsors have authorized and signed off on the most recent versions of all documents and that a contract exists prior to delivering any services. Assure compliance with FDA and Good Clinical Practice guidelines, PPD SOPs, personnel policies and procedures, PPD Exposure Control Plan, IATA, and other regulations regarding the transport of biological specimens.
During the initial review of the protocol, consult with internal groups and support staff regarding procedural and budgetary items and the necessity for changes due to any subsequent protocol amendments. Obtain other functions’ commitment to close gaps and address issues timely and effectively. Control, manage, and follow day-to-day activities during the course of the clinical trial to resolve any issues and answer queries.

Consult with BD and finance staff during initial project documentation review on standard services and costs, supporting RFP feasibility assessments. Advise on possible solutions if needed. Draft responses for proposals.

Education and Experience

Superior time management, planning, and organizational skills
Competent with specific computers and enterprise applications, including office productivity
Ability to program the IT system according to protocol requirements
Proven analytical skills
Demonstrated compliance with procedures and policies
Ability to perform multiple tasks effectively in a stressful environment
Extensive knowledge and experience in Project Management in Global Central Lab environment
Strong client relationship management skills
Ability to work effectively with multi-level teams

Able to communicate, receive, and understand information and ideas with diverse groups of people in a comprehensible and reasonable manner.

new_jobs.title: Principal Experience Operations Program Manager, Agentic AI
new_jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD101827

Position Overview

At Autodesk, we empower our customers to make anything. As AI reshapes how people create, design, and work, we are advancing the next generation of Autodesk Assistant experiences across our products. Delivering a cohesive, high-quality experience at this scale requires exceptional program management embedded directly in the work.

We are seeking an experienced Principal Experience Program Manager to join the AEC Experience Foundations organization. This role will be deeply embedded with the Autodesk Assistant design team, working alongside designers and leadership to drive the day-to-day program, maintain clarity on priorities, and ensure work moves fluidly through the broader product development process.

You will be the connective tissue between Design and its partners across Product Management, Research, Engineering, Analytics, Content, and the broader Autodesk design ecosystem. You will participate directly in the team’s working rhythms, build a substantive understanding of the work, and connect signals across plans, decisions, dependencies, and teams. This is not a role focused simply on facilitating meetings or tracking milestones. Success requires understanding what the milestones mean, anticipating the impact of change, identifying risk early, and proactively bringing the right people together to keep the program moving.

Reporting to the Director of Experience Operations, you will work as part of a broader program management and operations team while remaining dedicated to Autodesk Assistant. You will also partner closely with operations leads to identify friction in the development process and help evolve the practices that enable Design to contribute effectively at scale in a rapidly changing AI landscape.

Responsibilities

Drive the day-to-day design program for Autodesk Assistant, maintaining clear priorities, milestones, dependencies, capacity, design readiness, decisions, status, and risks across a complex, multi-product environment
Embed directly with designers and design leadership across planning sessions, stand-ups, design critiques, reviews, and share-outs; ensure these working rhythms are purposeful, effective, and evolve with the needs of the team
Build a deep working understanding of the program so you can connect decisions and signals across teams, identify downstream implications, surface conflicts or gaps, and proactively bring the right partners together to resolve them
Create strong connectivity between Design and Product Management, ensuring the design team has clear and current product priorities, roadmap context, requirements, and decision inputs needed to focus its work effectively
Coordinate design work through the broader product development process, partnering closely with Research, Engineering, Analytics, Content, and other program partners to ensure requirements, insights, dependencies, and deliverables move fluidly through the system
Anticipate program risks and friction before they become late-stage surprises; communicate impacts clearly, escalate through design leadership and the broader program team as appropriate, and drive follow-through on decisions and actions
Partner with Experience Operations and program counterparts to identify opportunities to improve development processes, team ceremonies, tools, and ways of working based on direct experience with the team and the work
Help the team balance near-term delivery with longer-term experience goals, supporting predictable execution while maintaining consistency and cohesion across Autodesk Assistant experiences
Keep user needs visible in product-development decisions by connecting research, analytics, and design intent into the program and making experience trade-offs explicit when business or technical constraints require them
Use AI fluently in your own work to improve quality and efficiency, and help identify opportunities for AI-enabled practices to increase the quality, scalability, and effectiveness of the design and product development process
Navigate Autodesk’s highly matrixed environment with urgency and initiative, building strong relationships across product teams, shared platforms, and the Autodesk design ecosystem, including partnership with the Weave design system team

Minimum Qualifications

7–10 years of experience in program management, design program management, product operations, or related roles supporting complex digital product development
Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional programs in large, matrixed organizations or similarly complex environments
Demonstrated ability to operate as an embedded program manager: close enough to the work to understand its substance, dependencies, and implications while maintaining the program systems required for reliable execution
Strong hands-on program management skills, including planning, milestone and dependency management, capacity and readiness tracking, risk management, decision tracking, status communication, and escalation
Working fluency with design and research processes, including design systems, prototypes, critical user journeys, qualitative research, testing, and the role of insight in product development. Design craft expertise is not required
Ability to work effectively with Product Management and Engineering partners and to understand technical constraints and concepts at the level needed to investigate implications, communicate dependencies, and connect technical decisions to the broader program
AI fluency, including regular use of AI tools to improve personal effectiveness and a demonstrated curiosity about how AI can improve product development practices, design workflows, quality, and scale
Excellent communication and synthesis skills, with the ability to translate complex and changing information into clear priorities, plans, risks, decisions, and executive-ready updates
Strong bias toward action, sense of urgency, sound judgment, and the ability to proactively build the relationships and context needed to move work forward

The Ideal Candidate

Bachelor’s degree in a related field preferred or equivalent practical experience
Is a program manager at their core: proactive, deeply engaged in the work, and motivated by making complex teams and programs function exceptionally well
Understands the difference between tracking a milestone and understanding it, including why it matters, what it depends on, and what changes when it moves
Builds a mental map of the organization and knows how to find the right person, context, or decision quickly rather than waiting for direction
Is comfortable operating in ambiguity and rapid change, particularly in AI product development, while still creating enough structure for teams to execute predictably
Can move easily between detailed program mechanics and the broader product and experience context without losing sight of either
Brings a user-centered mindset to program decisions and helps ensure research, analytics, and experience quality remain part of the conversation alongside business and technical considerations
Brings adaptability and initiative: sees what needs attention, connects the right people, and follows through until the issue is resolved
Operates with low ego and high accountability, partnering effectively within a larger program management and operations team rather than working as a standalone function

Learn More / Plus d'information

About Autodesk / À Propos D’Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Bienvenue chez Autodesk ! Nos logiciels créent chaque jour des choses extraordinaires : des bâtiments les plus écologiques aux voitures les plus propres, en passant par les usines les plus intelligentes et les films à succès. Nous aidons les innovateurs à concrétiser leurs idées, transformant non seulement la façon dont les choses sont fabriquées, mais aussi ce qui peut l’être.

Nous sommes très fiers de notre culture chez Autodesk ; elle est au cœur de tout ce que nous faisons. Notre culture guide notre façon de travailler et de nous comporter les uns envers les autres, influence nos interactions avec nos clients et nos partenaires, et définit notre image au monde.

En tant qu’Autodeskien, vous pouvez accomplir un travail significatif qui contribue à bâtir un monde meilleur, conçu et réalisé pour tous. Prêt à façonner le monde et votre avenir ? Rejoignez-nous !

Salary transparency /
Transparence Salariale

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For Canada based roles, we expect a starting base salary between $109,000 and $159,500. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. Belonging

new_jobs.title: Controls Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Company

STACK INFRASTRUCTURE (STACK) provides digital infrastructure to scale the world’s most innovative companies. We are an award-winning industry leader in building, owning, and operating highly efficient, cost-effective wholesale, colocation, and cloud data centers. Each of our national facilities meets or exceeds the highest industry standards in all operational categories of availability, security, connectivity, and physical resilience.

STACK offers the scale and geographic reach that rapidly growing hyperscale and enterprise companies need. The world runs on data. Data runs on STACK.

The Position

STACK is seeking an experienced Project Controls Manager to serve as a BMS & EPMS subject matter expert within the Innovation and Engineering team (I&E). This role is responsible for supporting the design and execution of Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) across STACK projects. The Project Controls Manager will partner with Preconstruction, Construction leadership, design teams, and OFCI vendors to establish, maintain, and govern controls requirements that support informed decision-making and successful project execution.

The Project Controls Manager will review design drawing packages prepared by Engineers of Record, evaluate mechanical and electrical equipment submittal packages, and coordinate requirements between design teams, construction teams, controls contractors, and equipment vendors. This role will work directly with construction teams throughout project execution and assist with commissioning activities to help ensure the installed controls systems align with the approved design and project requirements.

As the controls SME on the I&E team, this individual must have a strong understanding of the mechanical and electrical systems throughout the building and how those systems are monitored and controlled. The Project Controls Manager will review customer specifications, translate controls requirements to the appropriate project stakeholders, and work with design teams to ensure those requirements are incorporated into the project design.

Key Attributes

Ability to read, interpret, and review construction drawings, specifications, and technical documentation.
Strong understanding of mechanical and electrical building systems and their associated monitoring and controls.
Experience with BMS and/or EPMS systems; candidates with deep expertise in either mechanical or electrical controls are encouraged to apply.
Ability to review mechanical and electrical equipment submittals for controls-related requirements and design alignment.
Ability to review customer specifications and work with design teams to incorporate requirements into project documentation.
Strong understanding of the construction process and the coordination required between design, construction, vendors, and controls contractors.
Proficiency with construction management software and the ability to effectively navigate project documentation.
Self-driven, technically curious, and capable of operating as a subject matter expert while working across multiple project stakeholders.
Ability to independently interpret customer or owner requirements and work with design teams to translate those requirements into executable project documentation.

The Details

Location: Remote
Domestic travel required: up to 20-30%
Benefits: Healthcare, Dental Care, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Paid Leave Programs
Must be eligible to work in the United States
Must pass comprehensive background and drug screening

Must-have Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business administration, construction management, engineering, or a related field.
4+ years of experience in controls, MEP design, construction, commissioning, or a closely related field supporting complex facilities.
Experience working directly with design engineers, general contractors, controls contractors, equipment vendors, and construction teams through design and execution.
Experience with data center or mission-critical facility construction is highly desirable.
Working knowledge of the construction and commissioning process, including the ability to support issue resolution from design through turnover.

Compensation Range

$133,000.00 - $154,000.00

This Might Be Right For You If

You are a strong communicator, you are persuasive and clear, blending analytics with experience in decision-making.
You do not get flustered easily. You can juggle multiple priorities while balancing urgent requests with shifting timelines and deliverables.
You are a team builder. You take the time to understand and develop the strengths of your resources while formulating long-term plans for the growth and success of the team.
You are naturally curious and driven toward continual improvement. While you celebrate your successes, you take time to review and analyze campaigns for future learning.

WHY STACK?

We offer a competitive compensation package with strong benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, flexible spending accounts – even a cell phone subsidy.
We foster a culture of appreciation, including peer-to-peer recognition and rewards programs.
Fun is part of our DNA, with events, game nights, happy hours, and barbecues.
We’re growing – this is a great time to join and make an impact!

STACK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, national origin, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law

new_jobs.description:
DCS has an exciting opportunity for a Senior AOC Operations & Technology Program Manager
providing support to the Command, Control, Communications (C3C)/Kessel Run division.

Kessel Run is revolutionizing how the United States Air Force develops, deploys, and operates mission-critical software. We are seeking an experienced AOC Operations & Technology Program Manager to serve as the critical bridge between commercial airline operations control practices and military Air Operations Center (AOC) modernization.

This is a full-time remote position.

Position Contingent upon Contract Award**

Essential Job Functions

In this role, you will leverage deep commercial airline industry expertise—specifically from Airline Operations Control Centers (OCC / NOCC)—to advise and guide software product teams, operational leaders, and system architects. You will help translate battle-tested commercial concepts such as Collaborative Decision Making (CDM), real-time disruption management, automated flight dispatch, and predictive resource allocation into modern, cloud-native command and control (C2) software capabilities for the warfighter.

Duties Include, But Not Limited To

Commercial Aviation Practices & Operational Strategy

Champion the adoption of proven commercial airline Operations Control Center (OCC) processes, metrics, and workflows across Air Operations Center functional areas.
Introduce and adapt commercial Collaborative Decision Making (CDM) frameworks and Air Traffic Management (ATM) flow strategies to military airspace planning and dynamic air tasking.
Advise leadership on modern disruption management (irregular operations / IROP) models, crew/fleet recovery algorithms, and slot management concepts to improve operational resilience and sortie execution.

Product Roadmapping & Technology Modernization

Partner closely with product managers, software engineers, and user-experience (UX) designers to translate operational pain points into clear user stories, functional requirements, and product roadmaps.
Facilitate user-centered design sessions and workflow mapping between operational controllers, planners, and software development teams within an agile/DevSecOps development cycle.
Evaluate emerging commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) airline software, optimization solvers, and cloud architectures to determine feasibility for integration into modern AOC software suites.

Operational Metrics & Performance Optimization

Establish and monitor data-driven operational KPIs modeled after commercial aviation standards (e.g., departure punctuality, turnaround time optimization, asset utilization, and fuel/route efficiency).
Utilize operational telemetry and user feedback to identify planning bottlenecks, track system adoption, and quantify the operational impact of newly deployed software features.
Oversee capacity planning and operational modeling to support both day-to-day operations and surge tasking requirements.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Change Management

Serve as the primary operational liaison between software product teams, operational military leadership, acquisition authorities, and industry technology partners.
Drive change management initiatives that help traditional operations teams transition smoothly from legacy monolithic software and paper-based tracking to automated, cloud-based applications.
Prepare operational impact analyses, technical white papers, and business cases to justify modernization investments.

Travel may be required at the customer’s discretion up to 25%.

Position Contingent upon Contract Award**

Required Skills

Due to the sensitivity of the customer, U.S. citizenship is required.

Must be able to obtain a Secret Clearance.

Bachelor’s Degree in a related field in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed plus 12 years of experience.

5+ years of operational management experience within a major commercial airline, air cargo carrier, or airline operations technology provider.

OCC / Dispatch Background: Direct experience operating within or building technology for a commercial Network Operations Control Center (NOCC/OCC), Flight Dispatch, or Integrated Operations Center.
Aviation Domain Knowledge: Comprehensive understanding of flight operations, dispatch workflows, slot and flow management, disruption recovery (IROP), and crew/aircraft schedule optimization.
Leadership & Change Management: Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams, managing complex technical programs, and championing process change across operational workgroups.

Desired Skills

Commercial Aviation Software: Hands-on experience with modern airline operations software platforms (e.g., Sabre, Jeppesen, Amadeus, NAVBLUE, Carmen, or custom cloud-based OCC tooling).
Collaborative Decision Making (CDM): Working knowledge of FAA/Eurocontrol CDM programs, System Wide Information Management (SWIM), or Ground Delay Programs (GDP).
Agile / Software Factory Experience: Experience working inside an Agile/Scrum software development environment, product management discipline, or DevSecOps product team.
Military / Defense Familiarity: Familiarity with USAF Air Operations Centers (AOC), Air Tasking Orders (ATO), or joint airspace coordination is a plus, but not required.

Interpersonal Skills

Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to develop and present briefings to senior leadership
Strong analytical and organizational skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced acquisition environment
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within Government and contractor teams

new_jobs.description:
Responsibilities

Sabre Systems is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity Solutions Engineer/Program Manager
to oversee contractor activities for a new program and provide advanced expertise in maritime OT/ICS cybersecurity. The role is responsible for reviewing cybersecurity plans, waiver requests, and equivalency submissions, while maintaining overall accountability for program quality, performance, and communication with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).

Work Environment & Additional Requirements

Location Hybrid – National Capital Region
Hybrid work with on‑site presence required for classified work
Occasional CONUS travel

Key Responsibilities

Program & Project Management

Serve as the primary point of contact to the COR, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and traceability of all deliverables.
Lead and coordinate a distributed review team through subordinate managers and technical personnel, directing workload assignment, prioritization, capacity planning, and quality assurance.
Maintain status summary available to the COR and provide a comprehensive status report including workload metrics, aging reports, staffing changes, issues encountered and observed trends.
Utilize workflow systems, case management tools, throughput tracking, and quality management practices to support a high-volume regulatory review environment.

Cybersecurity Technical Review & Subject Matter Expertise

Conduct detailed technical reviews of cybersecurity equivalency requests, ensuring proper identification of the regulatory requirement, adequacy of the proposed alternative safeguard, and sufficiency of supporting evidence.
Evaluate whether proposed alternatives meet or exceed required security effectiveness and produce analyses that are technically sound, complete, and traceable.
Apply Government-provided methodologies, checklists, process guides, and decision matrices to develop preliminary recommendations of Approve, Approve with Conditions, or Deny.
Draft signature-ready correspondence summarizing technical justification, findings, and any recommended conditions.
Support technical assessment of complex or novel waiver requests and cybersecurity plans.
Provide Subject Matter Expert‑level support and serve as an escalation point for OT/ICS cybersecurity questions.
Deliver internal training on maritime OT/ICS cybersecurity and review methodologies.

Technical Capabilities

This position requires strong proficiency in

OT/ICS network architecture, segmentation methods, and security control design.
Industrial and maritime communication protocols such as Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, and NMEA 0183/2000.
Maritime operational systems including ECDIS, AIS, GNSS, cargo and ballast systems, terminal operating systems, cranes, and facility automation.
Application of NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-series guidance, and ISA/IEC 62443 standards to operational environments.
High-volume workflow management, throughput monitoring, aging analysis, and quality control practices for technical and regulatory review programs.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university (technical degree preferred). Equivalent OT/ICS experience may substitute for the Subject Matter Expert component.
Minium eight (8) years of hands-on OT/ICS cybersecurity experience applying frameworks such as NIST CSF and ISA/IEC 62443.
Four (4) years of project management experience including leadership, throughput management, quality oversight, and deliverable coordination specifically managing U.S. Federal Government projects.
Expert understanding of OT network architecture, segmentation, industrial protocols, and maritime operational systems.
Demonstrated experience evaluating OT/ICS cybersecurity designs and regulatory compliance.
Experience managing high-volume regulatory or technical review operations using workflow tools and analytics.
At least one cybersecurity certification that satisfies DoD 8140 SC‑A requirements (e.g., CISSP, CISA, CISM).
At least one advanced OT cybersecurity certification (e.g., GICSP).
Must have an active DoD Secret Clearance or higher. Must be a U.S. Citizen

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting maritime cybersecurity programs, Alternative Security Programs (ASPs), DHS, or U.S. Coast Guard operations, highly desired
PMP certification.
Additional OT/ICS cybersecurity certifications (GRID, GCIP, ISA/IEC 62443 credentials).
Experience managing fully remote and onsite teams of ten or more
Additional cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, CISA, or CGRC (if not already counted toward minimum requirements).

At Sabre Systems, LLC, compensation is based on factors such as location, qualifications, experience, and contract-specific requirements; however, final compensation will be determined by individual qualifications and applicable contract terms. The general salary range for this position is as follows $175,000.00 - $200,000.00

This requisition is not bonus-eligible, but we still welcome and value your referrals. At Sabre Systems, we encourage employees to refer exceptional candidates. If you have any questions about the referral policy or this position, please contact the Recruiting team.

Sabre Systems, LLC, has been providing innovative technological solutions and services for Department of Defense, Federal Civilian, and commercial customers for more than 35 years. new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Senior Portfolio & Program Manager, Operational Technology & Engineering is responsible for the integrated portfolio of Operational Technology & Engineering (OT&E) initiatives across controls, central monitoring, OT infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and automation, ensuring programs are sequenced, governed, funded, and transitioned to operations as one connected roadmap rather than as separate projects.

This role combines disciplined portfolio and program management with proven, hands-on expertise in industrial controls and operational technology, including how controls systems integrate across critical facilities. It does not replace technical owners: engineering owns design, architecture, and engineering acceptance, while this role owns portfolio governance, integration, and transition to operations, and recommends sequencing, funding, and prioritization decisions to leadership. This position collaborates with engineering, operations, cybersecurity, IT, network, architecture, finance, procurement, vendors, system integrators, and regional teams across Global Operations Excellence to deliver key initiatives such as GMCC and central SCADA, and to strengthen the reliability, security, and supportability of Equinix’s critical facilities.

Responsibilities

Maintain a single, current view of all OT&E initiatives, including scope, funding, dependencies, risk, and expected value
Run intake, scoring, and prioritization of new work against strategy, architectural standards, and capacity
Lead quarterly and annual planning, roadmap development, and investment cases, partnering with Finance on forecasting and variance reporting
Lead multi-team programs end to end, including integrated plans, critical paths, and phased global rollouts to site teams
Define and enforce stage gates and readiness criteria (design, security review, pilot, production)
Ensure programs conform to approved architecture and engineering standards, working closely with architecture and review boards
Run program governance, including steering committees, status cadences, RAID logs, and decision records
Creates clarity from complexity by turning strategy, competing priorities, and incomplete information into an executable roadmap
Balances pace, cost, technical quality, cybersecurity, and long-term supportability in program decisions
Translate technical detail into executive-ready narratives, dashboards, and decision requests
Manage vendor and integrator engagements, including SOWs, deliverables, and performance
Track benefits realization and report whether delivered programs achieved their intended outcomes.

Qualifications

Typically, 10+ years in program or portfolio management, including 5+ years leading complex technical programs
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, technology, or a related field is desired.
Nice to Have: PMP or PMI certification, P.Eng., Lean, or Agile certification; ITIL Foundation or ServiceNow experience
Experience managing concurrent programs with shared dependencies and constrained resources
Proven, hands-on expertise in industrial controls and operational technology within data centre or critical facilities environments
Brings solid controls and OT expertise to engage engineers as a credible peer, challenge plans, and recognize material technical dependencies, while respecting engineering as the technical authority
Technical knowledge of Building Management Systems (BMS), power monitoring, SCADA, telemetry, and OT/IT network segmentation, including how these systems integrate, sufficient to challenge estimates and technical plans and spot risk
Strong financial acumen, including budget ownership and business case development
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive decisions without direct authority
Experience with both stage-gate and agile delivery approaches
Excellent facilitation, negotiation, written communication, and executive presentation skills, able to influence in a global, matrixed environment without direct authority

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Principal Technical Program Manager

Overview

Business & Market Insights (B&MI), at Mastercard, helps organizations turn data into actionable outcomes by providing intelligence, analytics, and consulting capabilities that enable businesses to run more effectively, optimize performance, and identify new growth opportunities. B&MI empowers customers to make informed decisions, improve efficiency and profitability, and accelerate innovation through data-driven insights, predictive analytics, and market intelligence

Role

The Technical Program Manager (TPM), Program Governance drives execution excellence across B&MI’s technology portfolio by establishing governance frameworks, delivering portfolio insights, and enabling data-driven decision making. This role partners with engineering, product, operations, and business leaders to ensure strategic initiatives are aligned, risks and dependencies are managed, and delivery outcomes are transparent and predictable.

All About You

Plan, execute, and deliver projects from inception to completion
Partner across roles and teams to ensure dependencies and risks are identified, well understood, and managed
Manage and ensure the timely scoping, design, implementation, and release of complex features
Drive budget planning and business case execution
Deep knowledge of financial planning for Programs to help them track and ensure optimal focus on key initiatives
Proactively identify roadblocks and challenges, and brainstorm and execute contingency plans throughout project execution
Facilitate cross-functional alignment and accountability across engineering, product, operations, and business teams.

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:

Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in the US, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive base salary and may be eligible for an annual bonus or commissions depending on the role. Mastercard benefits for full time (and certain part time) employees generally include: insurance (including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, disability, life insurance); flexible spending account and health savings account; paid leaves (including 16 weeks of new parent leave and up to 20 days of bereavement leave); 80 hours of Paid Sick and Safe Time, 25 days of vacation time and 5 personal days, pro-rated based on date of hire; 10 annual paid U.S. observed holidays; 401k with a best-in-class company match; deferred compensation for eligible roles; fitness reimbursement or on-site fitness facilities; eligibility for tuition reimbursement; and many more. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is required plus a minimum of 8 years relevant experience; or Master's degree plus a minimum of 6 years relevant experience to meet managerial expectations.

CLEARANCE REQUIREMENTS:
Department of Defense Secret security clearance obtainable within reasonable time based on requirements. Applicants selected will be subject to a U.S. Government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Due to the nature of work performed within our facilities, U.S. citizenship is required.

Responsibilities For This Position

This specific PM requisition is focused on identifying an experienced candidate to lead and partner within a fast-growing portfolio that is developing critical and urgent mission system capabilities. Responsibilities will include management of active internal investments to achieve future business commitments, current program execution, validation of customer requirements, and overall team leadership. The PM will work in coordination with a strong Business Development and Engineering Technical Lead. The responsibility is career-defining. So is the opportunity. At General Dynamics Mission Systems, we invent the technologies, products and services, that help our nation’s heroes keep our nation safe. The work is so advanced, our teams regularly redefine innovation and excellence for the world. If you’re looking for a challenge, you’ve just found it.

As a seasoned team leader, you’ll use proposal plans and strategies to lead a team in developing, defining, and implementing cohesive, integrated program/product, subcontractor, and material plans, and business plans that achieve overall current and long-term objectives of the program/product, business unit, and division. The Program Manager will identify needed resources for projects, define and assign major program roles, lead the establishment of and sets integrated WBS-based budget and schedule baselines, and monitor work accomplished to baseline plans to ensure rate of work completion is sufficient to meet program/product schedules. We’ll rely on you to balance program risks and opportunities with executable strategies to meet technical requirements and budgets, as well as manage people who lead cross-functional program teams in matrix organization that are focused on the delivery of a product or computer-based system from design to release for customers.

What you’ll experience:

Technologies that aren’t just top-notch, they’re often top-secret

new_jobs.title: Sr. Principal Technical Program Manager, End-to-End Data Center Delivery
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is seeking a highly technical Senior Principal Technical Program Manager to lead end-to-end delivery of hyperscale data center capacity—from site strategy through customer-ready compute and GPU capacity, operational handover, and production go-live. This IC5-level leader owns the integrated delivery path across a complex portfolio of greenfield, expansion, and colocation programs. The role operates with broad autonomy, resolves high-impact technical and commercial tradeoffs, and aligns senior leaders and external partners around capacity commitments. Success requires deep fluency in mission-critical electrical systems, white-space infrastructure, structured cabling, fiber, network dependencies, commissioning, and operational readiness.

In this role you will provide strategic oversight and leadership for the construction of data centers by colocation providers, ensuring the completion of projects on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. Oversees the creation, review, and maintenance of documentation, including design review, commissioning, and problem-solving papers. Directs the implementation and oversight of quality control processes to ensure all construction activities meet design specifications and industry standards. Conducts strategic site walks and provides executive oversight and strategic leadership for the startup and commissioning phases of major data center projects. Identifies critical gaps in risk identification and mitigation and drives organizational-wide initiatives to address these gaps. Leads the role of primary point of contact between the company and colocation providers. Oversees the selection, negotiation, and management of contracts with external vendors, contractors, and suppliers, ensuring contract compliance and performance and construction activities align with the approved design plans and specifications. Oversees the installation of power, cooling, networking, and structured cabling systems.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Lead multiple complex, high-value hyperscale data center capacity-delivery programs from site selection and due diligence through construction, commissioning, infrastructure deployment, and customer go-live.

Own the integrated master schedule, capacity milestones, budget, risk and issue management, change control, recovery planning, and executive reporting.
Define and drive the cross-functional delivery strategy across Real Estate, Capacity Planning, Energy and Utilities, Design Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Network, Security, Infrastructure Deployment, Finance, and Data Center Operations.
Lead technical due diligence for prospective sites and colocation facilities, assessing utility availability, power-delivery timelines, fiber connectivity, permitting, constructability, physical constraints, and readiness to support forecasted compute and GPU demand.
Drive technical decisions and execution across critical electrical and low-voltage scope, including utility interconnects, medium- and low-voltage distribution, switchgear, generators, UPS, busway, RPPs, containment, structured cabling, fiber pathways, network rooms, and white-space fit-out.
Establish and govern technical design reviews, constructability reviews, submittals, acceptance criteria, and decision forums; identify and resolve cross-functional dependencies before they affect committed capacity dates.
Direct readiness of critical equipment, construction progress, commissioning, integrated systems testing, quality validation, punch-list closure, and final acceptance.
Ensure network, fiber, security, low-voltage, and server-deployment workstreams are sequenced and ready to safely energize, validate, and make capacity available to customers.
Manage strategic relationships and delivery interfaces with general contractors, design firms, equipment vendors, colocation providers, utilities, carriers, and other external partners.
Lead escalation and resolution of complex technical, schedule, commercial, and operational risks that span multiple organizations or programs.
Drive operational handover to Data Center Operations, including asset and configuration data, maintenance information, test results, warranties, training, documentation, residual-risk management, and ownership transition.
Establish repeatable delivery mechanisms, metrics, technical standards, and lessons learned that improve predictability, speed, cost, and quality across the regional data center portfolio.
Communicate clearly and credibly with technical teams and executive stakeholders on capacity commitments, schedule health, cost exposure, key decisions, risks, and recovery actions.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience in technical program management, project delivery, engineering, construction, infrastructure deployment, or operations within mission-critical environments.
5+ years of direct experience delivering hyperscale, cloud, colocation, or large-scale enterprise data center programs.
Demonstrated ownership of complex programs spanning early planning, design, construction, commissioning, technical fit-out, infrastructure deployment, and operational handover.
Deep working knowledge of critical electrical infrastructure, including utility interfaces, substations or switchgear, generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution, busway, RPPs, and data-hall power distribution.
Strong technical understanding of low-voltage and network infrastructure, including structured cabling, fiber systems, containment, pathways, network deployment dependencies, and security-system interfaces.
Experience managing integrated schedules, critical paths, budgets, scope changes, vendor performance, commercial risk, and executive-level communications.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, lead through ambiguity, make sound technical tradeoffs, and resolve issues across organizational boundaries.
Ability to travel up to 50% within the Eastern U.S., particularly across Northern Virginia/IAD.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, or Construction Engineering; Construction Management; or a related technical discipline.
Experience delivering high-density AI, GPU, HPC, or large-scale cloud capacity.
Experience with both greenfield and leased/colocation data center delivery models.
Expertise in commissioning, integrated systems testing, operational readiness, and customer capacity turn-up.
Experience leading regional portfolios or programs with multiple concurrent data center delivery workstreams.
Proficiency with Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira, SharePoint, or comparable delivery-management tools.
PMP, PgMP, CDCP, CDCS, or related mission-critical infrastructure certification.

Qualifications

Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements.

Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only
